name: r4-m01
statement: The cued Olmo-3 base's loops at T 0.6 reinforce themselves: each partly repeated block already in its own text (case lists, re-derivations, table rows) raises the chance of the next repeat, so the loop hazard at a position grows with how self-similar (zlib-compressible) the text so far is, and truncating samplers (top-p, min-p, low T) set how strongly that history feeds back; the base finishes more often from RL's prefix because that text is less self-similar, not because its mathematics is sounder.
scope: Covers the cued base Olmo-3-1025-7B on MATH-500 at T 0.6 (top-p 0.95 or 1.0) and truncated sampling at T 1.0 (min-p 0.1, top-p 0.95), where rule-A loops occur, including continuations from given prefixes (K_own, K_rl, K_fresh). It does not cover cap hits without loops (the T 1.0 / top-p 1.0 cap hits, the RL model's 16 cap hits with no loop), wrong finished answers, the harder 328 (loops not measured there), or the weight-difference cells. It claims difficulty and position act on the loop hazard only through the self-similarity of the text they produce; the items that concentrate cap hits on long problems are listed as conflicts.

imports.finding: The probability of repeating a sentence rises almost monotonically with the number of earlier repetitions in context, and high-probability sentences reinforce faster.
imports.how: This is the core dose-response: near-repeats already in the history raise the hazard of the next repeat, so a self-similar history leads to a loop.

imports.finding: Under top-p with threshold above 1/2 a loop position becomes deterministic once the loop token's probability reaches the threshold; pure sampling never locks.
imports.how: Explains why the sampler sets the feedback gain: under truncation, self-similarity that pushes repeat tokens past the threshold locks the loop, while T 1.0 / top-p 1.0 leaves an escape route.

imports.finding: Per-token probability of a repeated phrase rises with each repetition.
imports.how: Supports the step from block-level self-similarity to higher repeat probability, measured here by zlib ratio instead of n-gram counts.

explains.how: The base's own long prefix is already self-similar, so continuing it inherits a high loop hazard (38 loops), while RL's less repetitive prefix gives 48 finishes.

explains.quote: because the base's loops have periods of hundreds of characters
explains.how: The repeated units are whole blocks (case lists, re-derivations), which is the block-level self-similarity the mechanism uses, not short token stutters.
Removing top-p at T 0.6 lowers the feedback gain but keeps the low temperature, so loops fall from 92 low-ratio cap hits but do not disappear.

explains.quote: Truncating the tail at T 1.0 brings loops back
explains.how: Truncation removes the escape tokens, so the same self-similar histories that are harmless at top-p 1.0 lock into loops at min-p 0.1 or top-p 0.95.

explains.quote: Rule-A loops: 0 of 500 in either cell.
explains.how: At T 1.0 / top-p 1.0 the feedback from history to repeat probability never reaches a lock, so no rule-A loop forms even in long answers.

explains.quote: Restarting cap hits (up to 3 attempts) gives 414/500
explains.how: A restart clears the self-similar history, so the hazard resets and many looped problems finish on a fresh attempt.

conflicts.quote: T1 cap hits exceed T2's by 15.2 points in Q4
conflicts.how: The cued base's excess cap hits sit on the longest (hardest) problems, which looks like a direct difficulty effect; the mechanism has to say that difficulty acts only through longer, more self-similar text, and these items do not show that.

conflicts.quote: they are the long problems for both
conflicts.how: The base's cap hits fall on problems that are long for RL too, so problem length or difficulty explains them at least as well as self-similarity.

rival: Impasse or soundness account: the base loops when it reaches a mathematical impasse (a wrong or stuck derivation), so the hazard follows problem difficulty and whether the prefix is sound, and RL's prefix helps because it is correct. Two observations separate the accounts. First, within one problem, the account here predicts that the sample which later hits the cap was already more compressible in its first 3,000 characters, while the impasse account predicts no difference before the impasse. Second, deleting verbatim repeated lines from the base's own prefixes, which leaves the mathematics unchanged, should raise the finish rate under this account and leave it unchanged under the impasse account.

predictions.experiment: Within-problem early compressibility, cued base at T 0.6: does the sample that later hits the cap have a more compressible opening than a sample of the same problem that finishes?
predictions.recipe: File s3://pg-lineage-769063704696/results/rlneurons/r3/base-01/out/F_math500.jsonl (rln3_gen rows). Define ratio(s) = len(zlib.compress(s.encode('utf-8'), 9)) / len(s.encode('utf-8')) using Python zlib at level 9. Group rows by problem_index. A problem qualifies if it has at least one row with cap_hit true and at least one row with cap_hit false and len(text) >= 3000 characters. For each qualifying problem take C = the cap_hit true row with the lowest sample value and F = the cap_hit false row with len(text) >= 3000 and the lowest sample value. Compute rC = ratio(C.text[:3000]) and rF = ratio(F.text[:3000]). Score 1 if rC < rF, 0.5 if they are equal, else 0. Statistic: mean score over qualifying problems. Problems with no qualifying pair are excluded. Report the number of qualifying problems too.

predictions.experiment: Does pre-loop compressibility predict a later rule-A loop in cued base answers at T 0.6 / top-p 1.0?
predictions.recipe: File iterate-runs:abaybektursun-1114-151718-d4fa/answers.jsonl (run_cell rows, 500 MATH-500 answers). Keep rows with len(text) >= 6000 characters that either have loop_A false or have loop_A true with onset_A_char >= 7000 (rows with loop_A true and onset_A_char missing or below 7000 are dropped). For each kept row compute s = len(zlib.compress(text[:6000].encode('utf-8'), 9)) / len(text[:6000].encode('utf-8')). Statistic: AUROC of -s as a score for loop_A == true over the kept rows (Mann-Whitney form, ties count 0.5). Cap hits are not used as the label; only loop_A is. Report the number of kept rows and positives.

predictions.experiment: Is the cued base's opening text at T 0.6 more self-similar than RL's opening text on the same problem?
predictions.recipe: Files s3://pg-lineage-769063704696/results/rlneurons/r3/base-01/out/F_math500.jsonl (base, cue) and s3://pg-lineage-769063704696/results/rlneurons/r3/s2800-01/out/P_math500.jsonl (RL step 2,800, plain). Use only rows with sample == 0 in each file. Pair the two files by problem_index. Keep pairs where both texts have len(text) >= 3000 characters; problems missing from either file are excluded. For each pair compute rB = ratio(base.text[:3000]) and rR = ratio(rl.text[:3000]), with ratio(s) = len(zlib.compress(s.encode('utf-8'), 9)) / len(s.encode('utf-8')). Score 1 if rB < rR, 0.5 if they are equal, else 0. Statistic: mean score over kept pairs. Report the number of kept pairs.

predictions.experiment: Within each prefix kind of the RLN-4 K continuations, does compressibility of the stored text predict a cap hit?
predictions.recipe: Files s3://pg-lineage-769063704696/results/rlneurons/r4/modal_k-01/k_a/K_own.jsonl and .../k_a/K_rl.jsonl (rln4_gen rows; prefix_kind own_prefix / rl_prefix). Use the stored text field as it is. Keep rows with len(text) >= 3000 characters, and drop rows with loop_A true and onset_A_char missing or below 4000. For each kept row compute s = len(zlib.compress(text[:3000].encode('utf-8'), 9)) / len(text[:3000].encode('utf-8')). Within each file separately, compute the AUROC of -s as a score for cap_hit == true (Mann-Whitney, ties count 0.5); if a file has no cap hits or no non-cap rows after filtering, its AUROC is undefined and the statistic is the other file's AUROC. Statistic: the unweighted mean of the two AUROCs. Report each AUROC and its row counts.

predictions.experiment: Rerun the K_own arm of RLN-4 K on the same 78-problem pool (base-01 F cap hits that RL solved), with the same prefixes: cue plus the base's own first L tokens, cut before its loop onset, same L as K_own. Before continuing, delete from each prefix every line (split on '\n', stripped, at least 10 characters) whose stripped text already appeared as an earlier line of the same prefix. Then continue with the base at T 0.6 / top-p 0.95, total cap 16,384 including the prefix, K_own seeds 43,000,000 + i, H100, vLLM as in modal_k-01. Count continuations that finish without a cap hit.
predictions.refuted_by: 25 or fewer of 78 finish (no gain over the 23 of the unedited K_own arm beyond noise), or the finish gain is no larger on the half of prefixes where deletion removed the most characters than on the other half
